title: Meta-Cognitive Analysis: Evaluating Declarative and Procedural Knowledge in Datasets and Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper examines how two kinds of knowledge from metacognitive theory—declarative knowledge (“knowing that”) and procedural knowledge (“knowing how”)—affect the performance of large language models (LLMs). The authors argue that prior work lacked a systematic way to compare these knowledge types in datasets and models because they are difficult to define, separate, and measure directly.

To study the question, the paper introduces an in-context knowledge injection method. Using GPT-4 as a decomposer, the authors split question-answer reasoning into declarative hints, procedural hints, or a combination of both, and then evaluate 32 open LLMs on 13 datasets spanning arithmetic, commonsense reasoning, and broader knowledge tasks. The setup is not a human-subject or educational intervention; it is a model-analysis experiment using benchmark datasets and LLMs.

The main conclusion is that declarative knowledge usually provides larger gains than procedural knowledge across most tasks, while procedural knowledge helps more in simpler reasoning tasks such as elementary arithmetic and basic commonsense. The paper also finds that larger models and models with more pre-training steps are better at using both kinds of hints, especially declarative hints. The authors present these results as guidance for evaluating and improving LLM reasoning and knowledge use.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic large language model / generative AI system with no single named product focus.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper studies in-context knowledge injection into multiple LLMs rather than a single instructional product; the broader method and conclusions are about LLMs generally.

findings.finding_summary: Across 13 benchmark datasets and 32 open LLMs, the paper reports that declarative hints usually improve performance more than procedural hints, with procedural hints outperforming declarative hints only on simpler reasoning tasks. The authors summarize this as a general pattern in how LLMs utilize injected knowledge, but they do not report a single aggregate effect size or confidence interval.
findings.measure: Relative performance improvement from declarative hints, procedural hints, and combined hints versus no hint

quality_tier_rationale: This is a methodological paper about analyzing LLM knowledge types, not an education study or an evaluation of a K-12 instructional AI tool. It does not present a pedagogical intervention, randomization, or student outcome evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: No K-12 reading/literacy outcome is measured, and no effect size for instructional impact is reported. The paper’s results are about benchmark task performance of LLMs, not educational impact.
